brief: Goldman's consumer morning note leads with Nike (-8%), where a top-line miss and FY27 EPS guidance of $1.15-$1.35 (vs $1.68 consensus) landed close to what bears already expected, as a 26% ex-FX decline in Greater China overwhelmed +2% North America growth. Management's new Pace program targets $2.5bn in cumulative savings through FY31. The debate shifts to whether FY27 is the trough, though Goldman sees no clear evidence of that yet; applying a 25x multiple to the $1.25 guidance midpoint implies a $31.25 stock. Separately, tax-loss-selling pressure is building: GS's consumer short-candidate basket fell 9% in September, its second-worst month, and October carries a larger share of mutual-fund year-end selling than September, consistent with the prime book showing both discretionary and staples net sold. The broader prime positioning update shows the global book modestly net sold in September, short sales outpacing long buys in single stocks (1.2:1), and the US Consumer Discretionary long/short ratio at a one-year low of 2.06. The rest of the note is a factual roundup: overnight macro levels, September auto SAAR near 16.0mn, retail promotional checks with Buy-rated DKS and ASO, and Macau September GGR down 1% yoy, in line with expectations.
